id_routing.description: Interconnect may append bits to AxID to identify the originating master; slave-side ID_WIDTH > master-side ID_WIDTH
id_routing.compliance_note: Returning ID is the WIDER value; routing strips appended bits before returning to the master

fields.topology_type: Point-to-point master-slave serial; extensible to one-master + N-slave with per-slave SS lines.

supported_topologies.name: Point-to-point master-slave
supported_topologies.description: One master + one slave; 3 wires (MOSI/MISO/SCK) + optional SS.

supported_topologies.name: Multi-slave
supported_topologies.description: One master + multiple slaves; master uses one SS per slave (GPO); only one slave selected at a time.

supported_topologies.name: Multi-master
supported_topologies.description: Multiple masters share MOSI/MISO/SCK; mode-fault feature arbitrates bus access; SS doubles as collision-detect input.

responsibilities: Drive SS LOW (when SSOE+MODFEN active) before each transfer
Drive MISO on shifting edge while SS is LOW
Tri-state MISO when SS is HIGH

bidirectional_mode.description: When SPC0=1, single data pin is used; MOSI becomes MOMI (master) or MISO becomes SISO (slave). BIDIROE controls the direction of the chosen pin.

fields.interconnect_role: There is no protocol-layer interconnect (no router/bridge). Multi-slave is realized by per-slave SS routing in the SoC integration; multi-master is realized by shared MOSI/MISO/SCK with mode-fault-based arbitration.

ordering_guarantees.single_master_single_slave: Bytes are transferred in the order the master writes SPIDR.
ordering_guarantees.multi_master: No fairness guarantee; collision yields mode-fault and one master surrenders the bus.

ss_handling_per_topology.point_to_point_CPHA0: SS must toggle HIGH between bytes (min tI high time).
ss_handling_per_topology.point_to_point_CPHA1: SS may stay LOW continuously for back-to-back transfers.
ss_handling_per_topology.multi_slave: Each slave's SS individually driven LOW only when addressed.

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: Not applicable (no architectural memory map at the protocol layer).

slave_classification.duplex_slave: Capable of both transmit and receive; standard SPI slave.
slave_classification.receive_only_slave: Simpler slaves with no MISO output drive; master will not receive data from them.
